'''C. Marcella Carollo''' worked as a professional [[astronomer]] for 25 years between 1994 and 2019. Her scientific career was ended by the [[ETH Zurich|ETH Zürich]] who, following accusations that she had bullied students, made her the first [[Professor]] to be dismissed at ETH Zürich<ref name="20min.ch">{{Cite news |date=15 July 2019 |title=ETH entlässt Professorin nach Mobbing-Vorwürfen |language=German |work=20min.ch |location= |url=https://www.20min.ch/schweiz/zuerich/story/ETH-entlaesst-Professorin-nach-Mobbing-Vorwuerfen-20400772 |access-date=2019-07-15}}</ref> in the 165 years of its history. Carollo has maintained her innocence against these accusations,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencemag.org/sites/default/files/Press%20StatementMC.pdf|title=C.M. Carollo Press Statement of 31 October 2018}}</ref> publicly commenting on her case in terms that indicate "academic mobbing".<ref>{{Cite news|date=13 June 2019|title=Verfahren in der Gelehrtenrepublik|url= http://www.merkur-zeitschrift.de/2019/06/13/verfahren-in-der-gelehrtenrepublik|language=German|access-date=2019-06-13}}</ref> The dismissal was appealed unsuccessfully to the Swiss Federal Administrative Court.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Pfändler |first=Nils |date=2022-04-21 |title=ETH Zürich: Kündigung von Professorin war nicht missbräuchlich |language=de |work=Neue Zürcher Zeitung |url=https://www.nzz.ch/zuerich/eth-zuerich-kuendigung-von-professorin-war-nicht-missbraeuchlich-ld.1680260?reduced=true |access-date=2022-06-23 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220630180900/https://www.nzz.ch/zuerich/eth-zuerich-kuendigung-von-professorin-war-nicht-missbraeuchlich-ld.1680260 |archive-date=2022-06-30}}</ref>

== Education ==
Carollo began her studies at the [[University of Palermo]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://heritage.stsci.edu/2002/07/bio/bio_carollo.html|title=Carollo's Hubble Heritage webpage|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref> where she earned a [[laurea]] degree in physics in 1987, with a specialization in biophysics. She worked for more than four years outside of academia before starting a PhD in [[astrophysics]] at [[LMU Munich]], where she graduated in 1994.

== Career ==
Carollo was awarded a European Community Prize [[Postdoctoral fellowship|Fellowship]], which she held at [[Leiden University]] from 1994 to 1996. She held a [[Space Telescope Science Institute|Hubble Postdoctoral Fellowship]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stsci.edu/institute/smo/fellowships/hubble/fellows-list/|title=Space Telescope Science Institute listing of all Hubble Fellows 1990–2016|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=|archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20170220160434/http://www.stsci.edu/institute/smo/fellowships/hubble/fellows-list/|archive-date=2017-02-20|url-status=dead}}</ref> at [[Johns Hopkins University]] from 1997 to 1999. Carollo was appointed [[Assistant professor|Assistant Professor]] in the Astronomy Department at [[Columbia University]] in 1999, a position she held until 2002. That year, she moved to ETH Zürich as an [[Associate professor|Associate Professor]], in a dual appointment with her spouse [[Simon Lilly]]. She was promoted to Full Professor in 2007. She contributed as a member of the Science Oversight Committee to the development of the WFC3 camera<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stsci.edu/hst/wfc3/documents/handbooks/currentIHB/wfc3_acknowledgments.html|title=WFC3 Instrument Handbook|website=www.stsci.edu|access-date=2016-11-04}}</ref> which was installed on the Hubble Space Telescope in 2009. In 2012, she entered the Top Italian Scientist list from VIA Academy<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.topitalianscientists.org/top_italian_scientists_VIA-Academy.aspx?Cerca=carollo|title=Top Italian Scientists|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=|archive-date=2018-12-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181204101858/http://www.topitalianscientists.org/top_italian_scientists_VIA-Academy.aspx?Cerca=carollo|url-status=dead}}</ref> and in 2013 she was awarded the Winton Capital Research Prize.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wintoncapital.com/en/corporate-social-responsibility/winton-research-prizes|title=Winton Capital research prize recipients|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161021195627/https://www.wintoncapital.com/en/corporate-social-responsibility/winton-research-prizes|archive-date=2016-10-21|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2018, she was identified as a Highly Cited Researcher <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hcr.clarivate.com|title=Highly Cited Researchers|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190220122703/https://hcr.clarivate.com/|archive-date=2019-02-20|url-status=dead}}</ref> for her research work at ETH between 2006 and 2016 – one of only about 20 ETH scientists so recognized.

== Research ==
Carollo's contribution to astronomy is in the fields of [[extragalactic astronomy]] and specifically [[galaxy formation and evolution]].{{citation needed|date=July 2022}} Her early work established the relation between the [[metallicity]] gradient and stellar mass in [[galactic spheroid]]s, demonstrated the presence of [[dark matter halo]]s beyond their half-light radii and was seminal in discovering and characterizing disk-like (pseudo) bulges and nuclear massive [[star cluster]]s in [[disk galaxies]] like the [[Milky Way]].{{citation needed|date=July 2022}} Later she and her ETH group worked on the role of galactic environment and progenitor bias in galaxy evolution, the growth and "quenching" of massive galaxies at high [[redshift]]s, and participated in the discovery and characterization of the most distant galaxies in the universe, in the heart of the [[reionization]] epoch.{{citation needed|date=July 2022}}

== Controversy ==
From 2016 onwards, doctoral students and postdoctoral researchers at ETH Zürich’s former Institute for Astronomy lodged complaints with the university’s ombudspersons about Carollo’s supervision and leadership style. In 2017 the ETH Board instructed ETH Zürich to carry out an administrative investigation into the situation at the institute, while ETH itself dissolved the Institute for Astronomy and placed Carollo and her husband [[Simon Lilly]] on sabbatical leave; the closure and allegations were reported in Swiss and international media, including ''[[NZZ am Sonntag]]'' and ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]''.<ref name="Ruessli">{{Cite web |url=https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/main/news/eth-news/medienmitteilungen/2019/pdf/190410-Berichte/Schlussbericht-anonymisierte-Fassung.pdf |title=Bericht über die Administrativuntersuchung in Sachen ehemaliges Institut für Astronomie des D-PHYS an der ETH Zürich |publisher=ETH Zürich |date=3 October 2018 |language=de |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Donzé |first=René |title=Eklat an der ETH: Professorin mobbt Studenten |work=NZZ am Sonntag |date=21 October 2017 |language=de}}</ref><ref name="Science2017">{{Cite journal |last=Vogel |first=Gretchen |title=Swiss university dissolves astronomy institute after misconduct allegations |journal=Science |date=25 October 2017 |doi=10.1126/science.aar3257 |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/swiss-university-dissolves-astronomy-institute-after-misconduct-allegations |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref>

The administrative investigation was conducted by external lawyer Markus Rüssli and concluded with a final report in October 2018. The report found that Carollo’s leadership style and conduct towards subordinates conflicted with ETH regulations and internal codes of conduct, and characterised her behaviour as repeatedly disrespectful and personally harmful to staff. It recommended termination of her employment.<ref name="Ruessli" /><ref name="ETH2019report">{{Cite web |url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2019/04/investigation-report.html |title=ETH Zurich publishes investigation report |website=ETH Zurich |date=10 April 2019 |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref> Separately, on 17 January 2018 ETH Zürich opened an investigation into alleged scientific misconduct in connection with the case and suspended Carollo from her duties until the inquiries were concluded; this investigation was later closed without finding evidence of scientific misconduct, a point also noted by the Federal Administrative Court.<ref name="ETH2018misconduct">{{Cite web |url=https://ethz.ch/de/news-und-veranstaltungen/eth-news/news/2018/01/untersuchung-eingeleitet.html |title=Untersuchung eingeleitet |website=ETH Zürich |date=17 January 2018 |language=de |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bvger.ch/media-releases/38d39308-f9ff-41df-875f-5bd6f2aa3561/en/urteil_a-4744-2019_web.pdf |title=Urteil A-4744/2019 |website=Bundesverwaltungsgericht |date=6 April 2022 |language=de |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref>

On 31 October 2018 ETH Zürich announced that, on the basis of the administrative investigation, it had initiated formal dismissal proceedings against “a professor at the former Institute for Astronomy”, stating that the external investigation had identified “serious breaches of duty over an extended period” and recommended termination.<ref name="ETH2018dismissal">{{Cite web |url=https://ethz.ch/de/news-und-veranstaltungen/eth-news/news/2018/10/entlassungsverfahren-eingeleitet.html |title=ETH Zürich leitet Entlassungsverfahren ein |website=ETH Zürich |date=31 October 2018 |language=de |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref> In accordance with the ETH Professors’ Ordinance, a special committee of internal and external professors was convened to advise on the proportionality of dismissal. The committee confirmed the core findings of the investigation and deemed Carollo’s behaviour towards doctoral students unacceptable, but considered a dismissal legally problematic in view of the lack of earlier formal warnings and recommended instead that she be barred, at least temporarily, from supervising doctoral students and subjected to monitoring and coaching measures.<ref name="ETH2019report" /><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bvger.ch/media-releases/38d39308-f9ff-41df-875f-5bd6f2aa3561/en/urteil_a-4744-2019_web.pdf |title=Urteil A-4744/2019 |website=Bundesverwaltungsgericht |date=6 April 2022 |language=de |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref>

On 14 March 2019 ETH President [[Joël Mesot]] announced that the ETH Executive Board had nonetheless decided to request Carollo’s dismissal, citing the confirmed misconduct and a loss of trust as having destroyed the basis for continued cooperation.<ref name="ETH2019respect">{{Cite web |url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2019/03/measures-leadership.html |title="We should treat each other with respect" |website=ETH Zurich |date=14 March 2019 |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref> On 15 July 2019 the ETH Board (ETH-Rat) followed this request and decided to terminate her employment with six months’ notice, stating that it regarded the allegations against the professor as justified.<ref name="ETHBoard2019">{{Cite web |url=https://ethrat.ch/de/eth-rat-entlaesst-professorin-am-physikdepartement/ |title=ETH-Rat entlässt Professorin am Physikdepartement |website=ETH-Rat |date=15 July 2019 |language=de |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref> Carollo has consistently denied the allegations, describing herself as the target of an unfair campaign through statements by her legal counsel and in media interviews.<ref>{{Cite news |title=ETH Professorin wehrt sich gegen Vorwürfe |work=Nau |date=31 October 2018 |language=de |url=https://www.nau.ch/news/schweiz/eth-professorin-wehrt-sich-gegen-vorwurfe-65451312 |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=In Swiss Academic Science, Charges of Bullying and Gender Bias |work=Undark |date=8 May 2019 |url=https://undark.org/2019/05/08/marcella-carollo-ethz-gender-bias/ |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref>

Carollo appealed the dismissal to the [[Federal Administrative Court (Switzerland)|Federal Administrative Court]]. In April 2022 the court upheld the termination, holding that Carollo had over a period of years seriously violated important statutory and contractual duties through her conduct towards staff, so that a substantive ground for dismissal existed, and that the dismissal was neither abusive nor discriminatory under the Swiss [[Gender Equality Act (Switzerland)|Gender Equality Act]]. At the same time, the court found that ETH had failed to give an adequate prior warning and that the dismissal was therefore unjustified in the technical sense of federal personnel law; it awarded Carollo compensation amounting to eight months’ salary.<ref name="FACmedia">{{Cite web |url=https://www.bvger.ch/media-releases/38d39308-f9ff-41df-875f-5bd6f2aa3561/de/mm_a-4744-2019_dt_web.pdf |title=Gerichtsentscheid zur Kündigung einer ETH-Professorin |website=Bundesverwaltungsgericht |date=21 April 2022 |language=de |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pfändler |first=Nils |title=ETH Zürich: Kündigung von Professorin war nicht missbräuchlich |work=Neue Zürcher Zeitung |date=21 April 2022 |language=de |url=https://www.nzz.ch/zuerich/eth-zuerich-kuendigung-von-professorin-war-nicht-missbraeuchlich-ld.1680260 |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref>
